MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 11, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 5:00 p.m. and the City Council convened into closed session in the City
Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Potential Initiation of Ligation: One potential case

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR
  Government Code Section 54957.6
  City representative: City Council
  Unrepresented employee: City Manager

  ***
MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the Closed Session portion of the meeting at 5:55 p.m. and the City
Council took a brief recess for a reception honoring retiring Community Services Director Andy
Clark.

At 7:05 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL called the meeting back to order in open session in the City
Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Members of Los Hermanos Pacific Blue 2021 led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JUNE 11, 2019
   Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RESOLUTION OF COMMENDATION – ANDY CLARK, RETIRING COMMUNITY
  SERVICES DIRECTOR

MAYOR MITCHELL presented a Resolution of Commendation to Andy Clark in recognition of
his 21 years of service to the City of Rolling Hills Estates.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF and Equestrian Committee Member Carrie Silvano presented a
Certificate of Recognition to Andy Clark behalf of the Equestrian Committee in recognition of his
support of the equestrian community.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council.
  There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote.
  (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-D AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 28, 2019

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF JUNE 4, 2019

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – MAY AND JUNE 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61531 THROUGH 61567 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $159,310.06; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 050419 THROUGH 050519 IN

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 11, 2019
   THE AMOUNT OF $82,548.35 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $241,858.41
  WITH PROPER AUDIT.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT STUDY PRESENTATION

  Rick Espana, Roesling Nakamura Terada Architects and Leigh Kyle, Spurlock Landscape
  Architects provided an overview of the design process and presented the final design and
  cost estimates for the replacement of the George F. Canyon Nature Center building which
  includes a multi-level exhibit building, view deck and community room. He noted that the
  design process included input from the community, City staff and the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Land Conservancy staff.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the conceptual design as a guide for
  future development so that when funding sources become available the project can
  proceed.

  Discussion ensued concerning the conceptual design, the design elements incorporated
  to address traffic concerns and the additional costs associated with the multi-level exhibit
  building. COUNCIL noted general appreciation for the aesthetics of the concept design,
  but expressed concern regarding the estimated cost associated with the project and the
  availability of funding sources.

  Bridget Carman, Rolling Hills Estates resident expressed support for the project and
  stated that she is looking forward to development of this project.

  Paul Moylanen, Rolling Hills Estates resident expressed general support for the project
  noting that he is still concerned about cut through traffic.

  Ms. Kyle explained the design features that were incorporated into the parking lot design
  to address the traffic concerns.

  Further discussion ensued concerning options and suggestions for adjusting the design
  of the project to reduce costs. Following discussion and with COUNCIL concurrence, the
  following action was taken:

  APPOINTED COUNCIL MEMBERS ZUCKERMAN AND ZERUNYAN TO SERVE
  ON A SUBCOMMITTEE TO WORK WITH CITY AND PALOS VERDES
  PENINSULA LAND CONSERVANCY STAFF AND THE CONSULTANT TO
  REVISE THE PROJECT AND EXPLORE OTHER OPTIONS TO ADDRESS THE
  CITY COUNCIL’S CONCERNS REGARDING COST.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 11, 2019
 OTHER PUBLIC COMMENT:

Angie Gilbride, Cal Water, provided a construction update on the Palos Verdes Peninsula Water
Reliability Project.

Joan Davidson, PVE resident, expressed concern regarding the Butcher-Solana residential
development project in the City or Torrance and its impact on Ernie Howlett Park.

PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  GENERAL PLAN UPDATE – APPROVAL OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH MICHAEL BAKER INTERNATIONAL (MBI)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached Professional Services
  Agreement (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney) with Michael Baker International in
  the grand total amount of $755,600, which includes a $30,000 contingency for cost
  overages, to take over and complete the General Plan Update project.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the City make an effort to recover the
  $80,000 shortfall from the prior consultant. Following brief discussion, staff was directed
  to work with the City Attorney’s office to research the City’s options in this regard.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he is looking forward to working with
  MBI to completing the General Plan Update.

  John Bellas, Project Principal and Shane Burkhardt, Project Manager with Michael Baker
  International addressed the City Council to express their eagerness to work with the City
  in completing the General Plan Update.

  COUNCILMEMBER  ZUCKERMAN  moved,  seconded  by,  COUNCILMEMBER
  ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH MICHAEL BAKER INTERNATIONAL IN THE GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $755,600, INCLUDING A $30,000 CONTINGENCY FOR
  COST OVERAGES TO TAKE OVER AND COMPLETE THE GENERAL PLAN
  UPDATE PROJECT. (ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY)

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 11, 2019
 B.  ANNUAL AUDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement and rates for the CPA
  firm of Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP (RAMS) to perform CAFR audit for the
  Fiscal Year 2018-19, prepare the State Controller’s Cities Financial Transactions Report,
  prepare the Pepper Tree Foundation’s tax returns and review the GANN appropriation
  limitation.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Finance Director Whitehead stated
  that RAMS is currently working with the Cities of Rolling Hills and Canyon Lake as well
  as other larger cities.

  COUNCIL MEMBER  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE AGREEMENT AND RATES FOR
  THE CPA FIRM OF ROGERS, ANDERSON, MALODY & SCOTT, LLP TO
  PERFORM CAFR AUDIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2018-19, PREPARE THE STATE
  CONTROLLER’S CITIES FINANCIAL TRANSACTIONS REPORT, PREPARE
  THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION’S TAX RETURNS AND REVIEW THE GANN
  APPROPRIATION LIMIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

C.  APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT WITH ALL CITY MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR
  CROSSING GUARD SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement with All City
  Management Services for crossing guard services in the amount of $47,433.60.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).
  She clarified that the contract amount is $47,434.00.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Assistant to the City Manager Davis clarified
  that the service provided by All City Management Services is than that provided by the
  City’s part-time traffic control officers. She noted that The City’s traffic control officers
  control vehicular traffic flow on the City roadways while the crossing guards only control
  pedestrian traffic.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 11, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, second by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE AGREEMENT WITH ALL CITY
  MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR CROSSING GUARD SERVICES IN THE
  ANNUAL AMOUNT OF $47,434.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

D.  LOS ANGELES COUNTY ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL AGREEMENT RENEWAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Animal Control Services agreement
  with the County of Los Angeles for continued animal care and control services.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE ANIMAL CONTROL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES FOR CONTINUED
  ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL SERVICES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

OLD BUSINESS

A.  APPROVAL OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH VIGILANT SOLUTIONS FOR THE
  PURCHASE OF AUTOMATIC LICENSE PLATE READER CAMERAS AND
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH CITY OF TORRANCE FOR THE
  PURCHASE AND PLACEMENT FOR AUTOMATIC LICENSE PLATE READER
  CAMERAS PLACED ALONG SHARED BORDER.

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve: 1) the Public Works Contract with
  Vigilant Solutions for purchase of Automatic License Plate Reader Cameras in the
  amount of $122,241.59; 2) the Public Works Contract with Bear electrical for the new pole
  infrastructure in the amount of $10,800; and 3) Memorandum of Understanding between
  the City of Torrance and City of Rolling Hills Estates for the placement, operation and
  maintenance of Automatic License Plate Readers at two locations along shared border.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, Administrative Analyst Slawson stated
  that there are currently no poles located within the City or Rolling Hills Estates to support
  the expansion for desired neighborhoods; and it is more cost effective to use existing
  infrastructure in Torrance rather than install new poles.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JUNE 11, 2019
   In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding cost for the cameras,
  Administrative Analyst Slawson stated that the price point per camera is very competitive
  with the price paid for the initial cameras installed.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE FOLLOWING: 1) PUBLIC WORKS
  CONTRACT WITH VIGILANT SOLUTIONS FOR PURCHASE OF AUTOMATIC
  LICENSE PLATE READERS CAMERAS IN THE AMOUNT OF $122,241.59; 2)
  PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH BEAR ELECTRICAL FOR NEW POLE
  INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE AMOUNT OF $10,800; AND 3) MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF TORRANCE AND CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES FOR THE PLACEMENT, OPERATION AND
  MAINTENANCE OF AUTOMATIC LICENSE PLATE READERS AT TWO
  LOCATIONS ALONG THE SHARED BORDER.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz.

B.  REVISED WEED ABATEMENT OPTIONS FOR AMENDED AND RESTATED
  LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Select Option 3 to be implemented during the
  next five years of the Landscape Maintenance Services Agreement at a cost of $246,796
  annually; and 2) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an amended and restated Landscape
  Maintenance Services Agreement with Bennett Landscape with a term of five years
  starting July 1, 2019 for City Council approve on June 25, 2019.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).
  He further stated that since the staff report was published, there have been further
  discussions with Bennett Landscape where the proposal was clarified to be three phases,
  with varying prices per year, rather than three options; and staff is withdrawing its original
  recommendation. Given the current information, he stated that staff proposes the
  following options for Council consideration:

  1. Consider Bennett Landscape’s 5-year proposal as clarified;
  2. Determine if there is interest in the immediate termination of the use of chemical
  weed control measures and either request that Bennet Landscape submit a new
  proposal; or
  3. Direct staff to prepare and circulate a request for proposal to include the elimination
  of the use of chemical weed control measures.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that it was his understanding from the last
  meeting that the direction was to immediately discontinue the use of chemical weed
  control measures.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
JUNE 11, 2019
   MAYOR MITCHELL confirmed that was the direction provided, but it was her understating
  that Bennett Landscape was asked to present cost options and operational alternatives
  associated with the immediate cessation of chemical weed control measures. She asked
  Sean Bennett with Bennet Landscape to address the City Council.

  Mr. Bennett explained the challenges associated with immediately discontinuing the use
  of chemical weed control measures and provided information on the approach he
  proposes and the costs associated with that approach.

  Discussion ensued concerning Mr. Bennett’s revised proposal and the options before the
  City Council including issuing a request for proposals.

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL, City Manager Prichard clarified Mr. Bennet’s proposal
  and commented that another option before the City Council would be to seek proposals
  to include landscape maintenance with elimination of the use of chemical weed control
  measures and an expanded scope of service to include irrigation control. He suggested
  that the City Council may also consider exploring that option with Mr. Bennet’s firm before
  seeking other proposals.

  Following discussion and with CITY COUNCIL concurrence, the following action was
  taken:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO WORK WITH BENNET LANDSCAPE TO DEVELOP A
  COMPREHENSIVE COST PROPOSAL TO IMMEDIATELY ELIMINATE THE
  USE OF HERBICIDES AND EXPLORE THE OPTION OF ADDING IRRIGATION
  CONTROL TO THE AGREEMENT AND BRING A REVISED CONTRACT BACK
  FOR CONSIDERATION.

NONE.

JUNE 11, 2019
 A.  CONSIDERATION OF AN APPOINTMENT TO FILL AN UNSCHEDULED VACANCY ON

  Recommendation: That the City Council

  City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF commented that Mr. Martin has been very active in the
